what: The spec-producer declared a governances_loaded set carrying the format bars and the process governances but none of the three resolved-actor bars - oracle-spec, builder-spec, architect-spec - which spec-producer-governance names in the same sentence as the ones it did load, and which the spec-judge grades backward at this gate. The cold judge stopped at preflight and rendered no lens verdict. Loaded all three and ran the self-alignment pass they ask for.

Self-alignment against the oracle bar found an unbought surface element: the capability shipped an audit mode and a check mode differing by exit code alone, printing the same findings the same way. No actor wanted the list without wanting it fixed, and the sibling it was patterned on has two modes because it has two severities, which this one does not. Cut the flag; one mode, non-zero on any finding. The per-project wiring drops the flag with it.

A doubled-backtick span was skipped by regex accident rather than by rule, so the specification claimed to extract every inline-code path while the engine silently ignored a whole span form. Converted the accident into a stated rule - a doubled span exhibits markup rather than citing it - with its own scenario and a mutation proving the rule load-bearing. This also removed the need for suppression markers on the node's own illustrations.

Self-alignment against the builder and architect bars found the node carried no control-flow graph and no scenario map, so the suite was derived from a prose list rather than from a graph and could not surface a hole. Drew the graph, mapped every scenario to an edge, and enumerated the actors the capability serves. Drawing it exposed an unhandled edge: a named spec directory that is not there failed unhandled instead of being refused by name.

The engine excluded every doubled-backtick span outright, so a genuinely broken reference written that way escaped silently - reproducing inside the exclusion the exact looks-anchored-isnt failure the engine exists to close, and the suite could not tell that implementation from a correctly narrow one. Cut the exclusion and implemented the stated rule instead: code spans are delimited the CommonMark way, a run of N backticks opening and the next run of exactly N closing, so a span around another span is not a path while a span around a bare path is a reference however many backticks opened it. No exception, one escape hatch, and the hole closed rather than documented.

Four of the five use cases named the spec author as the invoking actor for rows that were state conditions encountered during someone elses run - scenario content in a use case's clothes. There is exactly one invoking actor, the per-project entry point, so the table collapsed to one use case whose divergences are extensions, and the stakeholders who feel the failure moved to the What section where they are not mistaken for callers.

Two scenario-map rows named the relative-prefix decision as the edge under test when the decision they actually exercise is the resolution failure. Restated the map's rule - the edge is the scenario's When, never a decision reached on the way there - and re-derived every row against it rather than patching the two named. A required What section was also absent; added, carrying the why, the stakeholders, and the non-goals.

A mutation sweep over the new code-span scanner found the run-length matching rule load-bearing but untested: ignoring the closing run's length failed no test, because no fixture carried a nested span followed by a path. Added the discriminating fixture and its scenario; the mutation now fails exactly one test.

The code-span scanner abandoned the rest of a line the moment it met a backtick run with no matching close, contradicting the node's own claim that spans are read as CommonMark delimits them. One stray backtick therefore hid every reference after it on that line - the engine's own looks-anchored-isnt failure class arriving by a second route, one round after the first was closed. An unmatched run is now literal text the scan resumes after, with its own scenario and a mutation that fails exactly one test. The judge's cited repro was not itself a demonstration: on that line the lone backtick pairs with the next one, which is correct CommonMark. The defect is real on a line whose unmatched run precedes a well-formed span, and that is the fixture the suite now carries.

The ignore marker was matched by unanchored substring, so any comment whose name began with the marker's - a typo, a future sibling - silently inherited its power to hide a reference. An escape hatch that fires on something other than itself is not explicit. Now matched as a complete comment, with the rule stated in the node and a scenario pinning that a prefix-sharing name does not suppress.

The ignore marker was tested against the raw line while every other extraction decision read only what sits outside the code spans. A line that merely quotes the marker therefore suppressed its own genuine references - and quoting it inside a code span is exactly how this node and its skill document the marker, so the design's most-guarded piece was self-triggering. The marker is now read from outside the spans like everything else: no exception for the escape hatch. Third instance in three rounds of one rule reaching further than its stated reason, which is the pattern rather than the individual bug.

Link extraction matched only the bare bracket-paren form, so a titled link, an angle-bracket-wrapped target, and a reference-style definition each silently extracted nothing while the spec said markdown link target without qualification. The judge ranked it advisory on zero corpus occurrences; taken as blocking anyway, because a silent miss is the failure class this CR exists to close and the corpus having none today is what the check is meant to keep true tomorrow. All four inline forms plus the label definition now extract, each mutation-proven load-bearing.
